result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A new supplier gets 30 unless you give a value, and `updateSupplier` changes it on renegotiation. The full offline suite passes: 608 tests, including a new one in `SupplierTest`. I did not commit.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: the `supplier` table has `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, with a check that it is not negative.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: `Supplier` has a sixth component, `paymentTermsDays`. The existing five-argument constructor is kept and defaults to 30, so the 78 existing call sites compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms. The listings by name, by country and by minimum rating, and `findSupplierById`, read them back.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: a new test covers the 45-day supplier renegotiated to 14 days, the 30-day default, and all four listings.

One gap to decide on: other queries that also return a `Supplier`, such as spending per supplier, supplier performance, purchased quantity per supplier, single-supplier categories and purchase suggestions, still build the supplier with the 30-day default. They will show 30 days even when the supplier has other terms. I left them alone because you listed only the four listings, but they need the same column added if those reports should show the real terms.
